title.narrative: UN Women Gender Responsive Budgeting Västra Balkan 2020 - 2024
UN Women Gender Responsive Budgeting Western Balkans 2020 - 2024

description.narrative: Overall goal: Project countries (Bosnia and Herzegovina, Albania, Kosovo, and Serbia) systematically integrate gender equality and become more transparent at all stages of national and local policymaking and budgeting processes. Outcome 1: National and local governments apply gender responsive budgeting to integrate gender equality principles in public financing processes Output 1.1: Ministries of Finance, Line Ministries and National Gender Equality (GE) Machineries have knowledge and evidence to make informed budgetary allocation towards GE in line with national, and international commitments Output 1.2: Local governments have the capacity to apply Gender-Responsive Budgeting (GRB) tools in their plans and budgets Output 1.3: Government officials share knowledge and best practices across the region on GRB Outcome 2: Public oversight bodies, women including the disadvantaged, demand transparency and accountability of public policies and budgets to gender equality processes Output 2.1: Parliament and oversight bodies have capacities to monitor and advocate for gender responsive policies and budgets Output 2.2: Gender equality advocates are able to raise issues related to Financing for GE Output 2.3: Women, including the disadvantaged, are able to voice their needs and act as agents of change in planning and budgetary process Output 2.4: Oversight bodies are able to share knowledge and best practices across the region on GRB

Insatsen är ett stöd till UN Women för projektet "Transformative Financing for Gender Equality towards more Transparent, Inclusive and Accountable Governance in the Western Balkans". Projektet implementeras av UN Women på västra Balkan (huvudsakligen i (Bosnien och Herzegovina, Albanien, Kosovo och Serbien samt regionalt). Det övergripande målet med insatsen är att stärka jämställdhetsintegrering i samtliga delar av budgetprocesser inom myndigheter och offentliga institutioner på nationell och lokal nivå på västra Balkan. UN Women arbetar tillsammans med ansvariga institutioner i länderna, såsom finansministerier, jämställdhetsmyndigheter och kommuner, liksom med media och civilsamhälle.

The contribution is a support to UN Women for the project "Transformative Financing for Gender Equality towards more Transparent, Inclusive and Accountable Governance in the Western Balkans". The project is being implemented by UN Women in the Western Balkans with country level activities in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, and Serbia. In addition, there is a regional component where also North Macedonia is part. The overall goal of the project is to enhance systematic integration of gender equality at all stages of national and local policy making and budgeting processes in Western Balkan countries. UN Women works with responsible institutions in the countries, such as ministries of finances, gender machinery, supreme audit institutions, municipalities, as well as media and civil society.

title.narrative: Agreement Sida-UN Women Gender Responsive Budgeting Western Balkans
Beslut om insats, UN Women Gender Responsive Budgeting Västra Balkan

description.narrative:
During 2020-2025, the Regional Gender-Responsive Budgeting (GRB) Programme contributed to strengthening the integration of gender equality into public policy and financing processes in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo and Serbia. The programme helped move GRB beyond awareness-raising and technical capacity development towards greater application in government planning and budgeting, stronger institutional and oversight mechanisms, and increased attention to the needs of women, including disadvantaged groups.
Outcome 1 National and local governments apply GRB to integrate gender equality in public financing processes The programme strengthened the capacity and readiness of government institutions to incorporate gender equality into public financing. GRB was increasingly integrated into national policy, legal and budget frameworks, supported by improved budget guidelines and instructions, gender analysis, gender budget tagging and sector-specific indicators. The evaluation found increased awareness and uptake among budget users and evidence that GRB was increasingly being applied in budget planning and to sector programmes. By 2024, 297 budget programmes mainstreaming gender were reported across the region. Importantly, the programme also supported the translation of GRB into local planning and budgeting, with 110 local governments adopting GRB policies or practices and 197 local initiatives applying GRB. These results indicate a shift from GRB as a policy commitment towards more routine application within public financial management, although the depth and consistency of implementation remain uneven.
Outcome 2 Public oversight bodies, gender equality advocates and women demand greater transparency and accountability The programme strengthened the accountability dimension of GRB, particularly through collaboration with Supreme Audit Institutions (SAIs). Oversight bodies conducted 130 monitoring initiatives on GRB implementation, and local governments subsequently acted on 86 recommendations from oversight institutions. This demonstrates an emerging accountability cycle in which gender-responsive budgeting is increasingly subject to scrutiny and government institutions are expected to respond. The programme also strengthened the capacity of oversight actors and contributed to greater parliamentary attention to gender-responsive budget information, although engagement with parliaments was more limited than with SAIs. Civil society and women's organizations were supported to articulate gender equality financing priorities, while 88 priorities of women from disadvantaged groups were reflected in planning and budgeting processes. Concrete examples indicate that GRB contributed to more responsive measures in areas such as social protection, health, agriculture, entrepreneurship and access to services.
Regional added value and sustainability Regional exchange strengthened knowledge, skills and professional networks among institutions working on GRB. The programme supported 61 regional learning events and the replication of 16 GRB practices. While the evaluation found limited systematic evidence of cross-country spill-over, post-programme evidence shows that relationships established through the programme have continued through informal and demand-driven exchanges. In particular, Ministries of Finance continue technical exchanges on gender budget tagging and integration of GRB into medium-term budget frameworks, while cooperation among SAIs has remained particularly strong. The formal regional platform has not continued after the end of dedicated funding, but the professional relationships and trust established through the programme constitute an important and potentially durable regional asset.
Results per country
Albania Albania is described as the most advanced and successful country for GRB, especially at the central level. The programme has been built on a long-standing UN Women partnership with the government and helped move GRB from an established policy requirement toward a more systemic component of public financial management. However, Albania does not yet have sufficient technical capacity to conduct systematic gender analysis of expenditure. Capacity at local levels is also a challenge. Summary of results -Gender-responsive budgeting (GRB) is fully integrated into national budgeting procedures. In 2025, 10.8% of national budget allocations were directed towards gender equality, following 10.0% in 2023 and 9.1% in 2024. -11 line ministries and 26 central institutions integrated GRB into the 20252027 Medium-Term Budget Framework, with 77 of 131 budget programmes incorporating gender-responsive measures. -GRB criteria are included in standard budget instructions, with dedicated GRB annexes and a Gender Budget Statement attached to the draft national budget since 2022. A Gender-Sensitive Citizens Budget has also been introduced. -Since 2024, GRB has been integrated into Public Investment Management, including assessment of the gender impact of public investments. -At local level, 45 local governments apply GRB policies and practices and all 61 municipalities use gender KPIs in budget planning. Gender tracking in 2023 identified 12% of local public finances as gender-responsive. -Oversight institutions conducted gender audits, including the first national gender audit on women's economic empowerment by the Supreme Audit Institution (ALSAI) in 2023. Albania's first gender audit methodology was developed in 2024.
Bosnia and Hercegovina (BiH) Bosnia and Herzegovina demonstrates the potential of GRB to work across a complex multi-level governance system, with particularly strong examples in Sarajevo Canton and Republika Srpska. The next challenge is to make these practices systematic and comparable across the country's different administrative levels. Furthermore, a transition from line-item budgeting to program-based budgeting - an overarching PFM-reform - is needed for GRB to become fully functional. This reform has been further delayed to 2027. Summary of results -Allocations for gender equality increased from 2% in 2020 to 4.54% in 2023. -In 2025, 14 governmental institutions across different levels of government mainstreamed gender in 27 budget programmes and increasingly used sex-disaggregated data and gender statistics in financial decision-making. -GRB was integrated into budget circulars at state and entity levels and in -Canton Sarajevo, while draft amendments to the Law on Financing of BiH Institutions were prepared to introduce mandatory GRB at state level. Canton Sarajevo prepared a gender-responsive 20262028 Medium-Term Budget Framework. -Three municipalities formally adopted GRB-integrated budget circulars by the end of 2024, with additional draft circulars prepared for adoption in 2025. -State- and entity-level Supreme Audit Institutions produced three SDG 5 audit reports, generating 27 recommendations covering more than 50 auditees.
Kosovo During the program implementation, GRB in Kosovo moved from being a relatively emerging practice toward formal integration into public-finance reform, legislation and local government planning. However, GRB remains to become institutionalised and there are several aspects of legal framework needed to be adapted, including PFM-reforms such as program-based budgeting. Summary of results -The Government approved the Concept Document on Gender-Responsive Budgeting in 2022, providing a basis for further GRB legislation and public-finance reforms. -A Gender Budget Statement was introduced, while GRB provisions were incorporated into ongoing reforms of the Public Finance Management and Procurement laws. -GRB was integrated into the 20252027 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, with 75 budget programmes mainstreaming gender. Since 2024, annual budget circulars include gender-equality considerations. -Five regulatory concept documents were reviewed through gender impact assessment, identifying 16 gender-equality policy measures and gender-sensitive indicators. -The 2024 Law on Social Housing provides for €3 million in institutional budget allocations to support survivors of violence through integrated services and employment opportunities. -16 municipalities adopted Gender Action Plans aligned with gender-sensitive MTBFs, while six updated their plans for 20242026. -The National Audit Office published two performance audits addressing gender equality and incorporated gender responsiveness into its Strategic Plan in 2024.
Serbia Serbia has demonstrated the broadest institutional coverage and a high degree of mainstreaming of GRB, building on a legal framework in which GRB has been embedded since 2015. GRB is widely embedded in government budgeting, linked to objectives and indicators, implemented locally and reinforced through extensive financial and performance auditing. The programme therefore focused on expanding sectoral implementation rather than establishing the basic legal framework. However, political developments and events during the program period significantly influenced governance responsiveness and focus on gender equality, limiting work on GRB. Summary of results -GRB is integrated into Serbia's national, provincial and local fiscal frameworks through the Budget System Law, Law on Gender Equality and Government Plan for GRB introduction. -In the 2025 budget, 81 of 89 direct central and provincial budget users (91%), covering 130 institutions, integrated gender perspectives into 118 programmes, 276 activities, 524 budget objectives and 924 indicators. -GRB integration increased from 83% of national and provincial direct budget users at the beginning of the programme. -14 local governments developed internal GRB procedures, including Annual GRB Plans and dedicated GRB teams. Measures addressed women's needs in rural development, entrepreneurship, tourism, youth, energy efficiency, climate change and cultural inclusion. - The Supreme Audit Institution conducted 118 monitoring initiatives, issued 61 recommendations, and published 119 financial audit reports on gender equality and one performance audit on GRB implementation. - The 2023 performance audit generated recommendations on sectoral gender analysis, reporting, implementation of the Gender Equality Strategy and costing of its Action Plan. The Action Plan was subsequently costed with programme support.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
